prompt:
Hana's closing the books for month-end and asked me to true up the rate-lock extension fees before they lock, because her booked totals don't match what actually cleared through payment processing. I set the extension pricing so the fee side sits with me. I've been buried in daily rate sheets and haven't had a clean look at the accounting, so take this end to end.

Start with Carlos's Rivera file (LN-2026-00619). That one had an extension attempt that bounced and then went through on a retry, and I want to be sure we're not double-counting the bounce and that only real money is on the books. Confirm exactly what cleared versus what merely got attempted. Then work through the rest of the extension fees Hana's already tracking for this close the same way, the ones she's got booked, placeheld, or flagged on her side. The Mercer new build (LN-2026-00184) is the worst of them with three separate charges. For each of those loans, line up what actually cleared on the payment side against what accounting has invoiced or billed, and don't let a failed-then-retried charge count as collected. If there are stray extension charges floating in payment processing that never showed up on Hana's radar and aren't tied to this close, they're not part of this pass, leave them alone.

Then flag every mismatch: amounts that don't agree between the two systems, extensions that cleared but were never booked, duplicate or inconsistent references, placeholder entries that were never trued up. Where a real fee cleared but never made it onto the books, book it the way we always book these extensions, as an operations extension-fee entry on the payables side, so the ledger reflects what actually cleared. If we clearly earned a fee but never charged the borrower for it, don't guess, flag it so we can decide whether to collect or write it off before close.

The Mercer file also has one extension where it was never settled whether the borrower or the builder is on the hook. I'm not making that call, it's above my pay grade. Lay out the details and flag it for Grace so she can decide.

When it's straight, email Hana a per-loan reconciliation: what cleared, what's booked, the difference, and what you booked or corrected. Copy Grace. Send Carlos the fee numbers on the two of his loans that are in this so he's not caught flat-footed if the borrower asks. And drop a short summary in the general channel listing the loan numbers that were off and which fees are still open, so nobody books against bad numbers going into close
